text:
Jon: @here seeing intermittent out-of-order packets in the us-west2 GPU pool. Streaming responses are stalling, GRPC deadlines firing.
Priya: Any pattern on which racks or NICs?
Jon: Looks concentrated on rack-r4 and r5 in usw2-azb. CPU + NIC counters spike at the same time.
Sam: Can you paste a tcpdump snippet?
Jon: Sure — short capture: 
```
15:22:10.123456 IP 10.12.4.5.52000 > 10.12.6.9.443: Flags [.], seq 12345..12407, ack 9876, win 31200, length 62
15:22:10.123457 IP 10.12.4.5.52000 > 10.12.6.9.443: Flags [.], seq 12307..12369, ack 9876, win 31200, length 62
```
Jon: Notice seq numbers arriving out of order (12407 before 12369) — small window reordering.
Anya: That matches the app logs — token stream stalls then a retry, which spikes GPU utilization and doubles cost for those requests.
Priya: Any packet drops reported? or just reordering/jitter?
Jon: No drops at kernel RX/TX level. NIC reports increasing GRO/LRO coalesces right when it happens.
Sam: Which NIC model? any recent driver updates?
Jon: On r4/r5 it's Mellanox MT27800 with mlx5 driver 5.18.0. We've got RDMA enabled for some hosts.
Priya: Could be RX steering/GRO + RDMA interaction. We've seen reordering when kernel coalesces then hands packets to XDP path out of sequence.
Anya: Can we reproduce with netem? or is this only in-prod when load spikes?
Jon: Tried a small netem reorder test in staging and saw similar stalls in the streaming path.
Sam: Quick mitigation suggestion: disable GRO on the affected NICs and measure. Command: `ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off`
Priya: That will increase packets/sec but may remove reordering. Worth a canary.
infra-bot: Scheduled maintenance window requested for usw2-azb racks r4,r5 at 23:00 UTC for NIC toggles.
Sre-oncall-bot: Alerting: increased GRPC deadline rate 2.3x over 10m — impacted routes: /v1/generate, /v1/stream.
Sam: Also check rdma device stats: `ibv_devinfo` and counter `rx_packets`, `rx_errors`, plus check `cat /sys/class/net/eth0/statistics/rx_missed_errors`
Jon: Ran `ibvquery` — no rdma errors but completion latency shows spikes correlating with reorders.
Anya: If disabling GRO fixes it, long-term we should tune NIC offloads or move RDMA VS workloads to dedicated subnet.
Priya: Another intermediate fix: enable `tcp_reordering` mitigation in the service: bump grpc keepalive and extend deadline by 100ms for streaming RPCs while we fix infra.
Jon: Doing a small canary: disabling GRO on two hosts and redirect a tiny percent of traffic via routing policy to test.
deploy-bot: Canary route change applied: 1% traffic -> host-azb-r4-02.
Sam: Please capture ethtool -k before/after and perf counters (softirqs, net_dev_queue) so we can compare.
Jon: Pre-change: `ethtool -k eth0` shows gro: on, lro: on, rx-checksumming: on.
Jon: Post-change (gro off): immediate drop in reorders for canary, GRPC deadline rate down to baseline for that shard. :thumbsup:
Anya: Good. Next steps: roll GRO off for the rest of r4/r5 during low-traffic window and monitor. If fixes persist, open infra ticket with NIC vendor for driver/firmware fix.
Priya: Also log cost impact in the incident note — retries increased GPU-minutes by ~18% for affected traffic in the last 6h.
Sam: Add a perf regression guard to catch sudden deadline spikes and auto-fall back to non-streaming endpoint (batch path) to avoid cost shock.
Jon: I'll attach captures and a short runbook in the ticket.
Anya: For longer term: evaluate XDP drop filters, firmware upgrade, or segregating RDMA-enabled hosts.
Priya: Assigning owners: @jon infra-side changes, @sam service-side backoff/guard, @anya vendor follow-up.
Jon: ETA rolling GRO change tonight 23:00 UTC, will report back in this thread.
infra-bot: Change executed on r4 hosts at 23:05 UTC.
Jon: Post-rolling: r4 and r5 show sustained low reordering, GRPC deadlines back to normal.
Sre-oncall-bot: Incident resolved: impact reduced to 0. Monitoring for 2h.
Anya: Filing vendor support ticket with Mellanox logs and packet captures (case #MLX-2026-334).
Priya: Thanks everyone — follow-up doc and cost delta to finance in the morning. :eyes:
Jon: TL;DR — Out-of-order due to NIC offload + RDMA interaction in usw2 racks. Temporary mitigation: disable GRO/GSO/TOS; long-term: firmware/driver fix or host segregation.
